interface.name: bande_shell_v1

description.summary: requests and events between the compositor and the shell

interface.description: Offered only on the connections of the shell clients the compositor starts itself (the shell and the screenshot tool), never on the listening socket.

request.name: activate_app

description.summary: bring an app forward

request.description: Focuses and raises the frontmost window of the app with this app id and raises its other windows behind it, as clicking a running app in the Taskbar does. Ignored when the app has no mapped window.

description.summary: the user pressed the launcher shortcut

event.name: capture_screen

description.summary: the user pressed the full-screen capture shortcut

event.description: Sent for Super+Shift+3, as Command-Shift-3 takes a picture of the whole screen on a Mac.

event.name: capture_area

description.summary: the user pressed the area capture shortcut

event.description: Sent for Super+Shift+4, as Command-Shift-4 lets the user drag out the part of the screen to take a picture of on a Mac.

event.name: active_app

description.summary: the app of the key window changed

event.description: Sent on binding and whenever the window with keyboard focus changes to one of another app, with that app's app id, as the macOS menu bar names the active app. An empty app id means no window has the keyboard, as when the user clicks the empty desktop.

event.name: volume_key

description.summary: the user pressed a volume key

event.description: Sent for the mute, volume down and volume up keys, with or without Super and also while the session is locked, as a Mac's volume keys always work. Fine is 1 when Option and Shift are held, which on a Mac changes the volume in quarter steps.

request.name: toggle_control_center

description.summary: open or close Control Center

request.description: Sent by the menu bar when its Control Center item is clicked. The compositor relays it to every shell client as toggle_panel.

request.name: set_icon_rect

description.summary: say where an app's icon is shown

request.description: Tells the compositor where the Taskbar shows the icon of the app with this app id, as a rectangle in the surface coordinates of the given surface. The compositor minimises the app's windows into this rectangle and restores them out of it. A width or height of 0 forgets the rectangle, as when the icon leaves the Taskbar. The rectangle is also forgotten when the surface is destroyed.

event.name: app_responding

description.summary: an app stopped or started answering

event.description: The compositor pings an app through xdg_wm_base whenever the user interacts with one of its windows, and every app with a window when Force Quit is opened. Sent with responding 0 when an app has not answered for 3 seconds, and with responding 1 when it answers again or exits. Also sent on binding for every app that is not responding, so Force Quit can mark it. Pid is the process on the other end of the app's connection, app id the app id of its windows.

request.name: hide_app

description.summary: hide every window of an app

request.description: Fades out every window of the app with this app id, as Hide in a Mac's Taskbar menu or Command-H does. The windows take no input while hidden. activate_app, activate_window or an activation request from the app shows them again.

request.name: quit_app

description.summary: ask an app to quit

request.description: Asks the app with this app id to quit, as Super+Q does: through bande_app_v1.quit_requested when the app has bound it, otherwise by asking each of its windows to close. The app may ask the user first.

request.name: force_quit_app

description.summary: end an app at once

request.description: Kills every process on the other end of a connection with a window of the app with this app id, without asking. Shell clients are never killed.

request.name: activate_window

description.summary: bring one window forward

request.description: Shows, restores if minimised, raises and focuses the window whose ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 identifier is given, as picking a window from a Taskbar icon's menu does. The Taskbar lists the windows, their titles and app ids through ext_foreign_toplevel_list_v1.

event.name: window_minimized

description.summary: a window was minimised or restored

event.description: Sent whenever the window with this ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 identifier is minimised (1) or restored (0), and on binding for every minimised window, so the Taskbar icon menu can mark minimised windows.

event.name: attention_requested

description.summary: an app wants the user's attention

event.description: Sent when an app asks to be activated without a valid activation token, for example when it finishes work in the background. The compositor does not raise it; the Taskbar bounces its icon instead.

request.name: set_corner_radius

description.summary: round the background effect of a surface

request.description: Rounds each blur region the surface set through ext_background_effect_surface_v1 with this radius, in surface coordinates, so a rounded Taskbar or menu blurs exactly behind its shape. 0 means square corners, the default.

event.name: focus_shell

description.summary: the user asked to reach a shell element from the keyboard

event.description: Sent with the layer namespace "taskbar" for Super+F3, "menubar" for Super+F2 and "menu-search" for Shift+Super+/, after the compositor gave the keyboard to the layer surface with that namespace or, when there is none, to the bar or the Taskbar. The client shows its keyboard selection. To give the keyboard back, for example on Escape, it calls activate_app with the active app.

request.name: show_app

description.summary: show the hidden windows of an app

request.description: Fades the windows of the app with this app id back in after hide_app, without raising them or moving the keyboard focus, as Show All in a Mac's app menu does.

event.name: brightness_key

description.summary: the user pressed a brightness key

event.description: Sent for the display and keyboard brightness keys, with or without Super and also while the session is locked, as volume_key is. Fine is 1 when Option and Shift are held, for quarter steps.

event.name: workspaces

description.summary: the row of workspaces changed

event.description: Sent on binding and whenever workspaces are added, removed or another one becomes active. Workspaces form one row, counted from 0 on the left; a full-screen window has a workspace of its own.

request.name: show_windows

description.summary: open the overview

request.description: Opens the overview of the active workspace. With an app id it shows only that app's windows on every workspace, as App Exposé does; an empty app id shows every window of the active workspace. Asking again for what is already shown closes it.

event.name: input_sources

description.summary: the keyboard input sources or the active one changed

event.description: Sent on binding and whenever the list of input sources or the active one changes. Sources is a comma-separated list of xkb layouts, each optionally followed by its variant in parentheses, such as "se,de(nodeadkeys)", in the order the user arranged them; active counts from 0.

request.name: select_input_source

description.summary: make an input source active

request.description: Makes the input source at this position of the list sent with input_sources active for the whole session. An index past the end is ignored.

event.name: media_key

description.summary: the user pressed a media key

event.description: Sent for the play/pause, pause, next and previous keys, with or without Super and also while the session is locked, as a Mac's media keys always control what is playing.

event.name: active_output

description.summary: the display holding the key window

event.description: Sent on binding and whenever the key window is on another display than before, with the name of that display's wl_output; empty when no window has the keyboard. The bar dims the active app's header on the other displays.

request.name: show_launcher

description.summary: open the launcher

request.description: Sent by the bar when its Bande mark is clicked. The compositor sends show_launcher to the shell clients, as Super+Space does.

event.name: open_launcher

description.summary: the user asked for one of the launcher's modes

event.description: Sent for Super+Shift+V (clipboard), Ctrl+Super+Space (emoji) and when an app asks for the emoji picker. Text field is 1 when the window that had the keyboard has an enabled text input, so that insert_text can type into it.

request.name: insert_text

description.summary: type text into the window the launcher covered

request.description: Commits the text through text-input-v3 into the text field of the window that gets the keyboard back after the shell surface closes, as the macOS character viewer inserts into the frontmost app. Dropped if no other client's text input becomes active within a second.

request.name: switch_workspace

description.summary: show another workspace

request.description: Slides to the workspace at this position of the row sent with workspaces on the display under the pointer, as clicking one of the bar's workspace dots does, and focuses its frontmost window. An index past the end is ignored.

entry.name: left
entry.summary: the left edge of the display

request.name: set_panel_anchor

description.summary: say where the item that opens a panel is

request.description: Tells the compositor where the bar shows the item that opens this panel, as a rectangle in the surface coordinates of the given surface, and on which display edge the bar lies. The compositor relays it to every shell client as panel_anchor in the coordinates of the usable area of that surface's display, so the panel opens beside its item.

event.name: panel_anchor

description.summary: where the item that opens a panel is

event.description: Sent on binding for every known anchor, whenever the bar reports a new one and whenever the usable area of its display moves, with the item's rectangle in the coordinates of the usable area of the display named by output (the area left beside the exclusive zones of bars, where a layer surface with an exclusive zone of 0 is placed) and the edge the bar lies on. An item inside a bar therefore has a negative coordinate on the bar's side. Control Center and the Notification Center open beside it, away from that edge.

event.name: full_screen

description.summary: a display shows a full-screen window or stops

event.description: Sent on binding for every display and whenever the active workspace of the display with this wl_output name becomes or stops being the space of a full-screen window. Full-screen windows are drawn above the top layer, so the bar moves to the overlay layer and hides until the pointer pushes against its edge.

event.name: displays

description.summary: the displays the shell draws on

event.description: Sent on binding and whenever a display is connected, disconnected, starts or stops mirroring another, or another display becomes the main one. Names is a comma-separated list of the wl_output names of the displays that show their own picture, the main display first. The shell puts a desktop and a bar on each of them.

request.name: set_scrim

description.summary: dim the display behind a layer surface

request.description: While this layer surface is mapped, the compositor dims the whole display behind it with the scrim colour at the given opacity (0 to 1), blurred where the renderer allows, so that a centred panel such as the launcher need only be as big as itself. A pointer press on the scrim reaches nothing below it: the compositor sends scrim_pressed instead. The opacity applies at once; send it right before the surface's commit to animate it with the surface.

event.name: scrim_pressed

description.summary: the pointer pressed on a scrim

event.description: Sent to the client whose layer surface set the scrim when a pointer button is pressed on the scrim outside the surface and its popups.

request.name: confirm_session_end

description.summary: ask the user before the session ends

request.description: Opens the confirmation for logging out, restarting or shutting down: the compositor starts the shell's session dialog as a shell client, or brings forward the one already open.

request.name: quit_all_apps

description.summary: ask every app to quit before the session ends

request.description: Asks every app with a window to quit, as quit_app does for each; apps with unsaved work may ask the user first. Windows of shell clients are left alone. From then on the compositor sends apps_running on this object until it is destroyed.

event.name: apps_running

description.summary: an app still holds a window

event.description: Sent after quit_all_apps and again whenever the answer changes: how many apps still hold a window, and the app id of the frontmost of them. A count of 0 means every app has closed its windows.

event.name: toggle_panel

description.summary: the user asked to open or close a panel

event.description: Sent to every shell client when the menu bar asks for Control Center or a keyboard shortcut asks for Control Center or the Notification Center. The client that draws the panel opens it, or closes it when it is open.

event.name: app_process

description.summary: the process behind an app's windows

event.description: Sent before the window list first shows a window with this app id, or shows a window's new app id, and on binding for every listed window. Pid is the process on the other end of the window's connection, so the shell can find the app a window belongs to when its app id names no installed app.

interface.name: bande_app_v1

description.summary: requests from the desktop to a whole app

interface.description: Offered to every client. A client that binds it takes over app-level requests that the compositor would otherwise express per window: while it is bound, the compositor sends quit_requested instead of closing each of the client's toplevels.

event.name: quit_requested

description.summary: the user asked to quit the app

event.description: Sent for Super+Q, as Command-Q quits an app on a Mac. The app should quit: close all its windows and exit, asking the user once first if something would be lost, as a terminal with running programs does. If the user cancels, the app keeps running and nothing is closed.

entry.name: left
entry.summary: the left half of the usable area

entry.name: restore
entry.summary: the size and place the window had before it was tiled or zoomed

entry.name: next_display
entry.summary: the next display, keeping its place there

request.name: place_window

description.summary: tile one of the app's windows

request.description: Places the toplevel as the window menu's Move and Resize items do, with the same animation and tiled states as dragging the window to a screen edge or pressing Ctrl+Super+Arrows. Restore undoes tiling and zoom. Zoom, full screen and minimise use xdg_toplevel's own requests. Ignored for a toplevel of another client and in full screen.

entry.name: next
entry.summary: the workspace to the right, a new one past the last

request.name: move_to_workspace

description.summary: move one of the app's windows to a neighbouring workspace

request.description: Moves the toplevel to the workspace beside the active one, as the window menu's Move to Workspace items do: the window slides off the screen and keeps its place and size there, and the keyboard goes to the next window. Moving past the last workspace adds one. Previous does nothing on the first workspace. Ignored for a toplevel of another client and in full screen.

request.name: set_keep_on_top

description.summary: keep one of the app's windows above the others

request.description: Sets or clears the window menu's Keep on Top toggle for the toplevel. While set, the window stays in front of every window without it on its workspace, even when another window is focused, and still below the menu bar, the Taskbar and other shell surfaces. Windows that keep on top stack among themselves by focus as usual. The state lasts until it is cleared or the window closes. Ignored for a toplevel of another client.

arg.name: keep
arg.summary: 1 to keep the window on top, 0 to stop

request.name: show_emoji_picker

description.summary: open the emoji and symbols picker

request.description: Sent by a text field's Emoji and Symbols item. The compositor opens the launcher's emoji mode as Ctrl+Super+Space does, and the chosen character is typed into the app's focused text field.

interface.name: bande_app_control_v1

description.summary: quitting apps and watching them answer, for Activity Monitor

interface.description: Offered to every client. It carries only what an app may already do to another app of the same user, politely: ask it to quit and learn whether it answers. It lists no windows and types no text. A client that binds it receives app_responding until it destroys it.

request.name: quit_app

description.summary: ask an app to quit

request.description: Asks the app with this app id to quit, as Super+Q does: through bande_app_v1.quit_requested when the app has bound it, otherwise by asking each of its windows to close. The app may ask the user first. Shell clients are never asked.

event.name: app_responding

description.summary: an app stopped or started answering

event.description: As bande_shell_v1.app_responding: sent with responding 0 when an app has not answered a ping for 3 seconds and with responding 1 when it answers again or exits, and on binding for every app that is not responding.
